Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:10:2.hebrew: בין מלא לחסר - סבורה היתה שיהא החדש חסר, וקבוע ביום ל', ולא יפול ביום החדש על פניו; והיה מלא, ולא נקבע עד יום שלשים ואחד, ולא נזהרה בו ביום ל', ונפל על פניו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:10:2.english: Between a full [month] and a deficient [month] - She thought that the month would be deficient and [the New Moon] fixed on the thirtieth day, so he would not fall upon his face on the day of the New Moon. However, [the month] was full, and [the New Moon] was not fixed until the thirty-first day; thus she was not careful regarding him on the thirtieth day, and he fell upon his face.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:11:1.hebrew: מבית אבי אבא - מבית אבי המשפחה, שבת נשיאים היתה, והם מבית דוד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:11:1.english: From the house of [my] father's father - From the house of the patriarch of the family, for she was a daughter of princes, and they are from the house of David.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:11:2.hebrew: חוץ משערי אונאה - לפי שצער הלב היא, וקרוב להוריד דמעות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:11:2.english: Except for the gates of [verbal] mistreatment - Because it is anguish of the heart, and [is] close to bringing down tears.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:12:1.english: One who mistreats the convert - [This refers to] verbal mistreatment.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:12:2.english: One who oppresses him - Presses him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:13:1.hebrew: לוחצו נמי תלתא כתיב ביה - וגר לא תלחץ, ולא תלחצנו, ולא תהיה לו כנושה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:13:1.english: [With regard to] one who oppresses him as well, three [prohibitions] are written concerning it - "And you shall not oppress a convert," "and you shall not oppress him," and "you shall not be to him like a creditor."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:13:2.english: You shall not be to him like a creditor - It is oppression, as he presses him to demand his debt.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:13:3.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: מאי שנא מאנה דכתיב ביה תלתא: "וגר לא תונה", "ולא תונו אותו", "ולא תונו איש את עמיתו", וגר בכלל עמיתו הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:13:3.english: This is the [correct] text: What is different [about] one who verbally mistreats [a convert], that three [prohibitions] are written concerning it: "And you shall not mistreat a convert," "you shall not mistreat him," [and] "you shall not mistreat, each man his colleague" — and a convert is included in "his colleague"?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:15:1.hebrew: מום שבך אל תאמר לחברך - כיון דגרים הייתם, גנאי הוא לכם להזכיר שם גירות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:15:1.english: A defect that is in you, do not say to your fellow - Since you were strangers, it is a disgrace for you to mention the term "stranger."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:15:2.hebrew: מאן דאית ליה זקיפ' בדיותקיה לא נימא לחבריה זקיף ביניתא - מיש שיש לו תלוי במשפחתו, לא יאמר לעבדו או לבן ביתו "תלה לי דג זה", שכל שם תלייה גנאי הוא לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:15:2.english: One who has a hanged [person] in his family should not say to his fellow, "Hang a fish" - Someone who has a hanged [person] in his family should not say to his servant or to a member of his household, "Hang this fish for me," for any mention of hanging is a disgrace to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:16:1.hebrew: אין מערבין פירות בפירות - בעל הבית שאומר, פירות שדה פלוני אני מוכר לך כך וכך סאין, לא יערבנו בפירות שדה אחרת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:16:1.english: One may not mix produce with produce - A householder who says [to a buyer], "I am selling you produce of such-and-such a field, so-and-so many se'ah," may not mix it with produce of another field.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:1:1.hebrew: עכנאי - נחש דרכו לעשות בעגולה, להכניס זנבו אצל פיו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:1:1.english: Akhnai - It is the way of a snake to form [itself] into a circle, bringing its tail by its mouth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:6:1.hebrew: כל טהרות שטיהר ר"א - על ידי מעשה שאירע, נשאלה הלכה זו בבית המדרש, שנפלה טומאה לאויר תנור זה, וחזרו ועשאו על גביו טהרות, וטיהרם ר"א, והביאום ושרפום לפניו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:6:1.english: All the ritually pure [items] that Rabbi Eliezer declared pure - Through an incident that occurred, this halakhah was asked [about] in the study hall, for ritual impurity fell into the airspace of this oven, and they subsequently prepared ritually pure [items] upon it, and Rabbi Eliezer declared them pure, and they brought them and burned them before him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:7:1.english: He wore black - A matter of distress and mourning.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:7:2.english: He too rent his garments - For an ostracized person is obligated to tear [his garments].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:7:3.hebrew: וחלץ מנעליו - שהמנודה אסור בנעילת הסנדל, במו"ק (דף טו:):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:7:3.english: And he removed his shoes - For an ostracized person is forbidden from wearing shoes, in Moed Katan (15b).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:7:4.english: And he slipped - from the chair.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:9:1.hebrew: ר"ג - נשיא היה, ועל פיו נעשה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:9:1.english: Rabban Gamliel - He was the Nasi, and [it] was done at his word.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59b:9:2.english: So that disputes will not proliferate - So that an individual will not make a habit of disputing the majority.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:11:1.hebrew: מבית אבי אבא - פי' בקונטרס: מבית דוד אבי משפחה, שבת נשיאים היתה, והם מבית דוד:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:11:1.english: "From the house of the father of [my] father" - Rashi explained: From the house of David, the father of the family, for she was a daughter of Nesi'im [the Patriarchs], and they are from the house of David.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:11:2.hebrew: חוץ משערי אונאה - "לפי שצער הלב היא וקרוב להוריד דמעות". משמע משום דנפקא לעיל מקרא דתהלים דשערי דמעה לא ננעלו, ובחנם דחק כן, דהא דריש לעיל רב חסדא בהדיא מדכתיב: "הנה ה' נצב על חומת אנך". ושמא מבית רבן גמליאל היתה מקובלת, שהיה אבי המשפחה, ולאו אדוד קאמר, כדאשכחן נמי (ר"ה ד' כה.) דאמר רבן גמליאל: "מקובלני מבית אבי אבא שפעמים בא בארוכה" כו':
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:11:2.english: Except for the gates of mistreatment - [Rashi explains:] "Because it is pain of the heart, and it is prone to bring down tears." This implies [that he explained it this way] because it is derived earlier from a verse in Psalms that the gates of tears are not locked. But he forced [this explanation] needlessly, for behold, Rav Chisda explicitly expounded earlier from what is written: "Behold, the Lord is standing upon a wall of plumb line [anakh]." And perhaps [she meant that] she received [the tradition] from the house of Rabban Gamliel [the Elder], who was the patriarch of the family, and she was not referring to [King] David, just as we also find (Rosh HaShanah 25a) that Rabban Gamliel said: "I have a tradition from the house of my father's father that sometimes [the new moon] comes by a long [path]," etc.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:14:1.hebrew: ואמרי לה במ"ו - יש מפרש, משום דחשיב "כי גרים הייתם" וכיוצא בה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:14:1.english: And some say in forty-six [places] - There is [one who] explains [that this is] because [this view] counts "for you were strangers" and similar [verses].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:1:1.hebrew: זה תנור של עכנאי - יש דגרס חכנאי, וכן בירושלמי, וחכן זה נחש. ושמא בעל התנור שהיה עושה, שמו כן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:1:1.english: This is the oven of Achnai - Some read Chachnai, and so it is in the Yerushalmi, and chachan means a snake. And perhaps the owner of the oven who made [it], his name was so.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:5:1.hebrew: לא בשמים היא - והא דאמר בפ"ק דיבמות (ד' יד. ושם ד"ה רבי) דהלכה כב"ה משום דיצאה בת קול, שאני הכא שבא לחלוק על דברי תורה, דכתיב: "אחרי רבים להטות"; אבל התם, אדרבה, ב"ה רובא, אי לאו דהוה מספקא לן אי אזלינן בתר רובא משום דב"ש הוו חריפי טובא. ועוד, דכאן לא יצאה בת קול אלא משום כבודו דר"א, שאמר: "מן השמים יוכיחו". והא דאמר התם: "רבי יהושע היא דאמר אין משגיחין בבת קול", ולא שמעינן ליה לר' יהושע אלא על ב"ק דהאי מעשה דר"א דהכא — התם דייק מדקאמר "לא בשמים היא, כבר ניתנה לנו תורה מסיני", משמע דבשום מקום אין משגיחין:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:5:1.english: "It is not in heaven" - And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Yevamot (14a, and there, s.v. Rabbi), that the halakha is in accordance with Beit Hillel because a Divine Voice emerged — here it is different, for [the Divine Voice] came to dispute the words of the Torah, as it is written: "After a majority to incline"; whereas there, on the contrary, Beit Hillel are the majority, were it not that we were in doubt whether we follow the majority because Beit Shammai were very sharp. And furthermore, here a Divine Voice only emerged for the honor of Rabbi Eliezer, who had said: "Let it be proven from Heaven." And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says there, "[This] is [the view of] Rabbi Yehoshua, who says we do not regard a Divine Voice," [even though] we only heard Rabbi Yehoshua [say this] regarding the Divine Voice of this incident of Rabbi Eliezer here — there [the Gemara] infers [this] from the fact that he said, "It is not in heaven; the Torah has already been given to us from Sinai," [which] implies that in no place do we regard [a Divine Voice].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:5:2.hebrew: קחייך ואמר נצחוני בני - והא דאמר בריש ע"ז (ד' ג:): "מיום שחרב בהמ"ק אין שחוק לפני הקב"ה" — היינו קבוע, והכא מילתא דבדיחותא בעלמא הוא דאמר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:5:2.english: "[He] smiled and said: My children have triumphed over Me" - And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says at the beginning of Avodah Zarah (3b): "From the day the Temple was destroyed, there is no laughter before the Holy One, Blessed be He" — that refers to constant [laughter], whereas here it was merely a lighthearted remark that He said.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:7:1.hebrew: וקרע בגדיו וחלץ מנעליו - אין להוכיח מכאן הא דמבעיא ליה במועד קטן (ד' טו: ושם ד"ה לא), אם מנודה צריך קריעת בגדים וחלוץ מנעל, דדלמא הכא לצערא בעלמא הוא דעבד הכי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59b:7:1.english: And he rent his garments and removed his shoes - One cannot prove from here that which is asked in Moed Katan (15b, and [in Tosafot] there, s.v. "Lo"), whether an ostracized person requires tearing of garments and removal of a shoe, for perhaps here he did this merely out of distress.
